notes.claim: A second earth fault on a different live conductor is a short circuit between active conductors through earth and the protective bonding conductors.
The Electrical Installation Guide says it is conventional to double the loop impedance of a circuit when working out a second fault.
The IEC 60364-4-41 text recommends that a first fault be eliminated with the shortest practicable delay.
BS 7671 sets requirements for a second fault on an IT system, similar to TN systems, in Regulation 411.6.4.

sources.title: IT system - Fault protection - Electrical Installation Guide
sources.quote: The second fault results in a short-circuit between active conductors (phases or neutral) through the earth and/or through PE bonding conductors (unless occurring on the same conductor as the first fault).

sources.title: IT system - Fault protection - Electrical Installation Guide
sources.quote: it is conventional to double the loop impedance of a circuit

sources.title: cdn.standards.iteh.ai
sources.quote: It is recommended that a first fault be eliminated with the shortest practicable delay.

sources.title: Wiring Matters - your insight into BS 7671
sources.quote: should a second fault occur on the opposite phase to the first fault there is potential for significant current to flow and, consequently, BS 7671 has requirements for protection against electric shock similar to TN systems; these conditions are covered in Regulation 411.6.4 of BS 7671.
